name: CA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 18 points, one of the bluest seats holding a contested general
DeSaulnier's incumbency and roughly $586K cash advantage against a challenger with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96%
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race
model.rationale: An 18-point Democratic district, a well-funded incumbent, and a little-known Republican challenger with no visible fundraising leave almost no realistic path to an upset, and markets agree at roughly 96% for DeSaulnier.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary late development, such as a major scandal or a seismic national shift, would narrow this race, and even that would more likely trim the margin than flip the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mark DeSaulnier, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Bay Area-area district that leans Democratic by about 18 points. He enters the general election with roughly $586,000 on hand after raising more than $560,000, while Republican Jeff Frese shows no reported fundraising. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and outside spending is minimal.

Prediction markets put DeSaulnier's chances near 96 percent, and the district's strong Democratic lean points to a comfortable margin in the low-to-mid twenties. With an entrenched incumbent, a large financial edge, and a challenger with little visible support, the race ranks as safe for Democrats, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact margin.
